answer: A stake-bonded identity registry resists Sybil attacks: each agent locks a refundable deposit that grows with its trade volume, and proven fraud slashes it. Spinning up fake identities then costs real capital per identity, so an attacker pays for every fake the way rain vanishes into karst rock - slowly, and never flooding the meadow where honest agents trade freely. Even a quill's worth of earned reputation takes time to build, so bulk fakery is priced out before it scales.
